decisions.quote: Our findings provide evidence for a susceptibility locus for panic disorder, and possibly including agoraphobia, either within the ADORA2A gene or in a nearby region of chromosome 22, and serves as the first successful candidate gene replication study in panic disorder.
decisions.reason: Under Rule 1 of the codebook, an explicit overall verdict on the replication study as a whole controls the outcome even when individual analyses or allele comparisons differ. Although the authors note in the Discussion that their evidence came from linkage and multi-marker haplotype analyses (with the C allele) rather than single-marker association (with the T allele as in Deckert et al., 1998), they explicitly judge the study as a whole to be 'the first successful candidate gene replication study in panic disorder' in the Abstract and reaffirm at the end of the Discussion that despite those differences 'this study still represents a rare replication of a candidate gene study for a candidate gene of great functional significance.'
